of: A mechanism by which a previously available course of action becomes unexercisable without its holder declining it and without any party at the holder's own table deciding about it, named with the condition lost (a permission, a capability, a counterparty, a coordination), the carrier that runs the clock, and the last intervention that could have kept it, and sorted by what the clock is made of, from clocks the holder never started to clocks the holder's own care for the option started: a closure that must strike before it can be known, a date on someone else's docket, a date on the option's parent, the holder's own development, the record's last witness, the world healing faster than the forum, a ratifier's term, a counterparty's transfer or planning cycle, a coordination's half-life, the holder's own growth, then the act that vests, the exercise that keeps, the readiness that spoils, the move on a neighbouring matter, the new state's first act, the machine that holds the option open, and the pause paper whose renewal belongs to the adversary.
map_register: Operator-grade and concrete: bank holidays and Sunday decrees, bar dates and opt-out postcards, emergency authorizations, eye patches, last-known-well times, mootness and class certification, adjournment sine die, memoranda of lease, reorganizations that absorb a vacancy, sixty-day signatures, approval ceilings, poured footings, empty flights and irrigated fields, thawed vials, first responsive pleadings, first writes, ECMO circuits and mine pumps, tolling agreements; drawn from capital controls, bankruptcy, public-health law, paediatrics, stroke care, constitutional litigation, legislatures, real property, employment, recall elections, mergers, land use, aviation and water law, cold-chain logistics, patent and civil procedure, software migration, transplant medicine, and litigation practice.

items.out: Bank holiday by decree: the option is shut by an authority whose shutting only works if nobody is told in advance, because the telling would itself be the cue to run, so the door is locked in the hours when the holder cannot reach it. Greece's banks stayed closed on Monday 29 June 2015 after a Sunday-night broadcast; Cyprus declared a bank holiday in March 2013 and kept extending it, once parliament had voted down the first levy, until the bail-in was on the statute book; Argentina's corralito was announced on a Saturday in December 2001; the export-licence suspension and the delisting are gazetted after they have taken effect. What is lost is a permission: the leave to move what belongs to you. The clock is the authority's own calendar, set to the Friday evening and the public holiday when the holder is locked out. The one act that could have kept the option was a transfer made on rumour alone, paid for by the chance of being wrong and by the discount the rumour market charges, and the deposits that left Greece that spring left on nothing firmer. So this is the single expiry on the map whose notice cannot come before it, and a holder waiting for a date is waiting for something the mechanism does not permit. Adds to runway-illusions' Cash behind glass, which books the deposit put into receivership on a Friday as owned and out of reach, the mechanism that picked the Friday. Not investor-tells' Let it lapse, a fuse the founder can test by letting it burn down, since a closure that can be probed is not one that has to arrive as a surprise; and not a withdrawn offer or a rival's foreclosure, which somebody at the holder's own table decides, since the decree is an authority's rule on a whole class and nobody at the holder's table decided anything about the holder. The item stands on that fence and on no claim that the exit dies as a by-product, because the decree names the exit and forbids it.

Notice by publication: the claim runs out on a date set in a proceeding the holder is not in the room for and is legally presumed to have read. The bankruptcy court fixes a bar date for proofs of claim and notices unknown creditors by putting it in the paper; the class settlement's opt-out deadline arrives on a postcard indistinguishable from junk mail; the probate creditor's window opens and shuts once the notice has run in the county paper. What is lost is a permission: the standing to be paid, or to sue on one's own account. The clock is the bar-date order joined to the rule of constructive notice, under which publication counts as knowledge for everyone the debtor could not name. The one act that could have kept the claim is a one-page proof of claim or a signed opt-out, the cheapest filing the law knows and the one least often made, because the holder who would make it is, by definition, the one nobody told. Adds to runway-illusions' Stamp's clock, a permission whose date the holder can read on the stamp, the date that is written on someone else's docket and imputed to the holder. Not deal-deaths' Missing witness, since nothing is missing from the record; only the holder is missing from the room.

Parent instrument lapses: the option was issued under a parent paper that has a term of its own, so it ends when the parent ends, on its own merits or none, and with no date printed on the grant itself. The emergency-use authorization ends when the declaration it was issued under is terminated, a separate paper from the public-health emergency that ended in May 2023 and left the authorizations in force; the cross-state telehealth licence lapsed as each state's emergency lapsed through 2021 and 2022; the wartime power, the pilot run under a waiver, the sub-lease that dies with the head lease. What is lost is a permission. The clock is the parent instrument's date, which the holder never signed and may never have read, because the grant it did read carried no date, so the holder's first job is to find which parent paper carries the term. The one act that could have kept it is conversion: full approval, a permanent rule, a licence in the holder's own name, filed while the parent still stands. Conversion is slow enough that it has to be started while the emergency looks endless, which is precisely when nobody starts it. Not Bar date in the newspaper, where the date sits on a docket and is imputed, since here the date sits on a different paper from the option and is honest; and not lead-time-floors' Calendar with nothing in it, a wait the rule imposes, since here the rule does not wait but ends.

Occlusion window: the option expires on the holder's own developmental timetable, which the holder cannot know, so the last intervention is by necessity in somebody else's hand. Amblyopia is most correctable by patching the good eye in the first years of life and responds less, and less completely, after about seven, though the trials of the 2000s found response into the early teens; the clubfoot is cast in infancy; the second language acquired without an accent, which is disputed as a hard window; the duckling imprinting on its first day. What is lost is a capability: the cortex's willingness to rewire. The clock is the developmental schedule, and the holder is a child who does not know there is an eye at stake. The one act that could have kept it is a screening, the preschool vision check and the parent who notices a squint, so the option belongs to one person and its preservation to another; where no screening programme exists, the option expires unseen at a rate that belongs to the programme, not to the child. Adds to Last known well, where a witness dates the option, the case in which the option's holder cannot be its own witness at all. Not a use-it-or-lose-it, since nothing the child does or fails to do runs the clock.

Witness clock: the option is dated by the last person who saw the fact, not by the fact itself, so it expires when the proof runs out while the tissue might still permit it. The stroke patient who wakes with the deficit is ineligible for thrombolysis because the four-and-a-half-hour window counts from when she was last seen well, which was bedtime, so the wake-up stroke loses the drug no matter when the artery actually closed; the same rule governs the opened vial with no time on the label and the sample with a gap in its chain of custody, both treated as expired at the earliest moment they could have been. What is lost is a capability: a treatment the protocol now forbids. The clock is the protocol's timestamp rule, which asks for a witness and not for the tissue. The one act that could have kept it is a witness: someone awake, a time written on the vial, or a witness of another kind, the imaging that reads the tissue's own clock, by which the WAKE-UP trial of 2018 gave the drug back to patients with no witnessed onset. Adds to witness-architectures, which asks what has to exist for a trace to form, the option that dies for lack of a trace while the fact would still allow it. Not Patch before seven, where the body's own clock has run, since here the body's clock may not have run and the record's has.

Moot before ruling: the option to have a decision expires because the situation resolves itself faster than the forum that would decide it can move, so nobody declines and nobody rules. The student's challenge to a law school's admissions was dismissed as moot because he was about to graduate (DeFunis, 1974); the pregnancy is over before the appeal; the election is held before the ballot-access case; the tenant is evicted before housing court sits; the employee's grievance is mooted by the reorganization that abolished the post. What is lost is a permission: the justiciability of the claim. The clock is the ratio of the forum's pace to the harm's duration, a number nobody at the table sets. The one act that could have kept it is a structure that outlives the individual harm: the class certified before the named plaintiff's harm ends, which Sosna (1975) allowed, or the doctrine that a harm capable of repetition yet evading review can be decided anyway, which Roe rested on; so the option is kept by a coordination or by a rule, never by hurrying. Not deal-deaths' Cost of the last mile, where the surplus is eaten along a curve, since here nothing is eaten and the harm is simply over; and not Bar date in the newspaper, since there is no date anywhere.

Adjournment sine die: the body that could have said yes reaches the end of its own term with the matter still pending, and its successor never has to say no. Bills die on adjournment sine die and must be reintroduced from scratch; the treaty is signed and waits on a parliament that is dissolved; the permit application sits before a council that is re-elected; the approval the old board agreed in the hallway and had not yet minuted when the board was reconstituted at the meeting; the offer approved by a committee that is disbanded in the reorganization. What expires is the matter's place in the process, because the successor body starts it from zero. What is lost is a counterparty: the specific body whose yes was on offer. The clock is the ratifier's own calendar, its election, session, or term. The one act that could have kept it is the vote scheduled before adjournment, the carry-over motion, the approval minuted rather than agreed in the hallway. The treaty cases are simplified, since most unratified treaties were eventually refused by someone; the clean form is the legislative bill, which dies by the thousand every session with no recorded no. Adds to deal-deaths' Ratifier's other deal, where the ratifier wanted a different bargain, the ratifier that wanted this one and was gone before the vote. Not Landlord changes, where the counterparty is replaced by transfer, since here it is replaced by the calendar.

Unrecorded promise: an option held in a person rather than on the paper that transfers expires at the counterparty's next transfer, which the holder neither controls nor, often, sees. The landlord who promised the renewal sells the building to a buyer not bound by unrecorded promises; the 'we'll take you back' comes from a manager who leaves; the side letter with a fund's partner has never been seen by the fund's successor manager; the supplier's verbal priority vanishes with the account executive. What is lost is a counterparty: the one whose word held the option. The clock is the register, the deed, the fund agreement, the offer letter on letterhead, none of which ever had the option written on it, so the successor takes free of it. The one act that could have kept it is recording: a memorandum of option on the title, a side letter countersigned by the entity, the promise put onto the paper that binds successors, which costs the awkwardness of asking a friendly counterparty to bind their unknown replacement. Adds to term-sheet-powers' Successor in the chair, where the replacement exercises a term the friend would not have, the mirror case, in which the replacement declines to honour a term the friend gave. Not Chair grown over, where the counterparty stays and the shape goes.

Vacancy absorbed: the option to return rests on a vacancy the counterparty has not yet re-planned, so it expires at the counterparty's next planning cycle with nobody declining the return. The leave taken with no return date whose post is split among three people at the next reorganization; the budget line reallocated at year end; the supplier's line retooled for the customer who stayed; the co-founder's seat the remaining founders stop leaving empty at the next hire. What expires is the return to the seat, since employment there afterwards is a fresh negotiation from the outside. What is lost is a capability on the counterparty's side: the shape that could receive the holder. The clock is the counterparty's planning cadence, quarterly, annual, the next reorganization, which sets the expiry with no reference to the holder at all. The one act that could have kept it is a dated return, a leave rather than a resignation, a reservation the cycle has to respect, or the return itself before the cycle turns. Adds to traces-of-the-unlived's Vacancy tenant, where preparing for a future breeds its opponents, the case in which nobody opposes the return and the absence is simply absorbed. Not forms-of-return's Reentry burn, a road open and hostile one way, since this road has closed.

Signatures past sixty days: an option that needs many simultaneous yeses expires unless the gathering outruns the decay of each yes, so a coordination has a half-life. The recall petition whose signatures older than sixty days are void under Michigan's rule, or which must all fall inside California's hundred and sixty days; the tender offer's minimum condition that has to be met by the offer's expiry; the crowd in the square that goes home; the reunion that becomes impossible one death at a time. What is lost is a coordination. The clock is the validity window on each act of assent, written by the rule or by the assenter's own attention span. The one act that could have kept it is a gathering rate: paid circulators, a date agreed in advance, a pact that binds the early yeses until the last one arrives. The recall and tender cases are observed; the crowd is analogy. Adds to who-can-be-bound's Place in line, an ordering lost by leaving, the coordination lost by others' leaving. Not Session ends, where one body's calendar kills the matter, since here many small calendars do.

Priced past the acquirer: the holder's own growth carries the counterparty out of reach, so the option to sell to the natural acquirer expires at the round that prices the company above what the acquirer can pay at all, a market capitalization smaller than the price, a wage cap, a fund's concentration limit, and past those a board's approval ceiling, with nobody at either table declining. The company whose preference stack now exceeds the largest deal any of its three strategic buyers has ever done; the player whose wage outgrows every club in the league but two; the practice too large for any partner to buy into and too small to list. What is lost is a counterparty: the buyer whose capacity was the option. The clock is the acquirer's capacity, legible in its market value and its deal history, set against the holder's own price, which every round raises. The one act that could have kept it is the sale at the last price under the ceiling, which was never seen as the last, or a round sized to stay under it, which is the one choice a founder is never advised to make. Analytical, since every observed case can be read as a buyer that would have paid more, so the item stands as a mechanism and not a count. Adds to market-deaths' Slowed past the rot, where a market thins from the outside, the market for the holder that the holder thins by growing. Not Chair grown over, where the counterparty re-plans, since here the counterparty is unchanged and the holder has left its range.

Footings before the vote: a permission is about to be withdrawn by a third party's change of rule, and it can be kept only by an act in the world that no filing substitutes for. The building may proceed under the old zoning only if the developer has substantially begun in reliance on a valid permit before the ordinance passes, the footings poured the week of the council vote; the nonconforming use survives the new code only if it is actually in use on the effective date; the grandfathered rate is kept only by the account that was open. What is lost is a permission. The clock is the code together with the vested-rights doctrine, which in most states vests on construction begun and in a few, Washington among them, on a complete application, so the last act differs by jurisdiction and the holder who knows which one has a different week. The one act that could have kept it is the hole in the ground before the vote, which is an exercise begun rather than a filing made, so the option can be preserved only by starting to use it. Adds to first-mover-forecloses, which holds the rival who changes the rules on purpose, the rule that changes for reasons of its own. Not Slot flown empty, where the exercise has to be repeated to keep the right, since here one beginning vests it for good.

Eighty percent or returned: the permission expires by disuse and is kept only by exercise, so the clock runs while the holder does nothing and stops when the holder acts, and the preserving act is the exercise stripped of its purpose. The airport slot must be flown eighty percent of the season or handed back, which had airlines flying empty aircraft in early 2020 until the rule was waived; the water right under prior appropriation is forfeited after five years without beneficial use, which has fields irrigated in a drought to keep them; the trade mark is abandoned after three years' non-use; the mining claim is kept by annual labour; the department budget is spent in the last quarter so it is not cut. What is lost is a permission. The clock is the regulator's usage ledger. The one act that could have kept it is the empty flight, which costs the full price of using the option and returns nothing but the option, so that keeping and using become one act and the option's upkeep is its exercise price. Adds to runway-illusions' Stamp's clock, whose licence lapses without hours logged and whose clock no cash extends, the price at which it can be extended after all, the hours flown for nobody. Adds to tollgates-that-must-buy's Stamp with an expiry, where the gate must spend its stamp, the permission-holder who must burn the permission to keep it; and to power-trades' Leased strike, where disuse makes a power unbelieved, the disuse that forfeits it by rule. Not Pour the foundation, one act that vests, since here no act ever finishes the keeping.

Pot life begins at mixing: preparing to exercise the option starts a decay the unprepared state did not have, so the option to wait expires because the option to act was made ready. The vaccine vial keeps for months frozen, for weeks once thawed, for hours once punctured; the epoxy's pot life begins at mixing; the drawn dose; the armed fuze; the reagent brought to room temperature; the opened surgical field; the reserve army that cannot be held at the frontier through the harvest it was drawn from. What is lost is a capability: the good itself, spoiling in its ready state. The clock is a chemistry, or a season, that starts at preparation. The one act that could have kept it is not preparing, or preparing in the smallest unit, the single-dose vial, the small mix, the tranche thawed for the day's bookings, so the clinic that thaws a whole tray to be sure of serving whoever walks in has bought readiness with the doses it will throw away at closing. The mirror of Slot flown empty, where the option dies of not being touched, since here it dies of being touched, and a holder who holds both must burn the one and refrain from readying the other. Not lead-time-floors' Understudy, a finished copy waiting, since the understudy does not spoil for having been rehearsed; and not Kept on the machine, where the harm falls on the holder and is billed by the day, since here it falls on the good.

Waived by the first response: the option must be taken before any other move on a linked matter, so its clock is the holder's own next act rather than a date, and a holder who does nothing keeps it while a holder who does anything adjacent loses it. The objection to the court's jurisdiction over the defendant is waived if omitted from the first response; the patent is dead in Europe on the morning of the conference talk and a year later in the United States; the appeal is waived by taking the settlement; the election of remedies; the defect in the goods that has to be objected to before the goods are used; the 'speak now' at the wedding. What is lost is a permission. The clock is a rule that ties the option to a position in a sequence, and the sequence is written somewhere other than the option, in the rules of procedure, the patent statute, the sales code, so the holder learns the order from the loss. The one act that could have kept it is the ordering itself: the provisional application filed the morning of the talk, the reservation written into the first filing, the objection lodged before the goods are unpacked, each costing nothing but the knowledge that an order exists. Not Slot flown empty, where the holder's inaction runs the clock, since here inaction is the only thing that keeps it; and not Bar date in the newspaper, since there is no date and the holder is the only one who can strike.

First write in the new shape: the option to reverse a move expires at the first act the new state performs that the old state cannot read, so the window is the pause between the change and its first consequence, and it closes with nobody deciding to close it. The migration can be rolled back until the new service writes its first record in a shape the old schema rejects; the merger is reversible until the first combined payroll; the new address until the first piece of mail arrives there; the reorganization until the first hire is made into the new chart; the currency changeover until the first contract is written in the new unit. What is lost is a capability: the old state's ability to take over from here. The clock is the first write, performed by the new state in the ordinary course of business and not a decision about the reversal at all. The one act that could have kept it is the expand-and-contract shape, writing to both for a season so the old can still read, at the price of running two and of a season in which neither is the truth. Adds to pivot-invariants, which name the retained assets that make leaving cheap, the moment at which one of them is lost; and to undo-costs, which bills a reversal that remains possible, the reversal that stops being possible. Not Thawed to be ready, where readiness spoils the good, since here the new state's use closes the way back to the old.

Bridge that ends the crossing: the option is held open by a device or an upkeep whose own running accumulates a harm or whose stopping is one-way, so the deadline is the machine's and not the situation's. The patient on ECMO as a bridge to transplant becomes ineligible for the transplant the circuit was keeping her alive for, because bleeding, infection, and clotting rise with each week on circuit and centres set a duration past which candidacy is reviewed; the mothballed mine kept dry by pumps whose stopping floods the workings past reopening; the ship in the reserve fleet whose hull is kept by cathodic protection that a budget line can end; the interim chief who has run the company past the point at which the search can bring in an outsider. What is lost is a capability: the eligibility, or the workings. The clock is the bridge itself, its complication rate or its upkeep bill. The one act that could have kept it is a listing at the moment of cannulation, a search begun the day the interim was named, a decision to stop pumping taken while a sale was still possible, each of which treats the bridge's start as the option's deadline. The ECMO limits are centre practice and are simplified. Adds to lead-time-floors' Bridge, a degraded replacement priced by the hour, the bridge that ends the option it holds open. Not Standstill with a term, where the clock is a date the counterparty signs, since here the clock is a harm nobody signs.

Tolling agreement's twelfth month: a pause taken to keep an option open is written on a paper that carries a date, so a situation that had no deadline acquires one, and the paper's renewal belongs to the counterparty, who now knows what the pause is worth to the holder. The tolling agreement stops the limitations clock the holder could have stopped alone by filing, and runs out in twelve months unless the adversary signs again; the negotiated leave of absence puts a date on a job that had none, and is extended only if the employer signs; the forbearance agreement holds the lender's foreclosure for ninety days; the furlough's recall rights run six months; the standstill in a takeover keeps the bidder from buying shares and ends on the day it says. What is lost is a permission: the leave to remain in the paused state. The clock is the pause's own instrument, and its clock is the only one in the situation the holder wrote. The one act that could have kept it is the renewal asked for before the counterparty learns it is needed, or a pause written without a term, which is rarely granted, the Korean armistice being the exception that has no renewal date and is still called temporary. The statutory pauses, the twelve weeks of the family-leave statute and the restraining order's fourteen days, are the same date without the mechanism, since the term is a rule's and the renewal belongs to a court or to no one, so the holder gets the deadline without paying the counterparty for it; those are runway-illusions' Stamp's clock. Adds to impasse-inventions' cooling-off right, reversibility offered as a chip, the bill the chip carries. Not lead-time-floors' No-shop, which serializes the search, since here the search is stopped and the stopping is what expires.
